question.prompt:
In a narrow alley of width \(w\) a ladder of length \(a\) is placed with its foot at a point \(P\) between the walls. Resting against one wall at \(Q,\) a distance \(k\) above the ground, the ladder makes a \(45^\circ\) angle with the ground. Resting against the other wall at \(R,\) a distance \(h\) above the ground, the ladder makes a \(75^\circ\) angle with the ground. The width \(w\) is equal to

[Figure 1](figures/1982_AMC_12_Q22_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The foot \(P\) stays fixed between the walls. Thus the two horizontal distances from \(P\) to the walls add to the alley's width.

A ladder of length \(a>0\) making angle \(\theta\) with the ground has horizontal reach \(a\cos\theta\) and vertical reach \(a\sin\theta\). Applying these right-triangle ratios to the two positions gives
\[
w=a\cos45^\circ+a\cos75^\circ,
\qquad
h=a\sin75^\circ.
\]
We therefore want to compare \(\cos45^\circ+\cos75^\circ\) with \(\sin75^\circ\). The difference formula is useful because \(75^\circ-45^\circ=30^\circ\):
\[
\sin30^\circ
=\sin75^\circ\cos45^\circ
-\cos75^\circ\sin45^\circ.
\]
Using \(\sin30^\circ=\frac12\) and \(\sin45^\circ=\cos45^\circ=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\), this becomes
\[
\frac12
=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}
\bigl(\sin75^\circ-\cos75^\circ\bigr).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\sin75^\circ-\cos75^\circ
=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}=\cos45^\circ.
\]
Substituting into the width expression yields
\[
w=a\bigl(\cos45^\circ+\cos75^\circ\bigr)
=a\sin75^\circ=h.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{h}\), choice \(\boxed{E}\).
solutions.title: Add the horizontal projections

solutions.explanation:
The two ladder positions have equal length, so joining their upper endpoints creates an isosceles triangle. The angles at \(P\) make this triangle especially useful.

Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be the points on the ground directly below \(R\) and \(Q\), respectively, with \(R\) on the left wall and \(Q\) on the right wall. Since \(X,P,Y\) lie on a straight line,
\[
\angle RPQ=180^\circ-75^\circ-45^\circ=60^\circ.
\]
Also, \(PR=PQ=a\). An isosceles triangle with vertex angle \(60^\circ\) has all three angles equal to \(60^\circ\), so triangle \(PQR\) is equilateral. In particular, \(QR=PR=a\).

Draw the horizontal segment from \(Q\) to the left wall, meeting it at \(S\). The ray \(QP\) is \(45^\circ\) below the leftward horizontal. Since \(R\) lies to the left of \(Q\) and \(\angle PQR=60^\circ\), the ray \(QR\) must be \(15^\circ\) above that horizontal. Thus \(R\) lies above \(S\), and
\[
\angle SQR=15^\circ.
\]
In right triangle \(RXP\), the angle at \(P\) is \(75^\circ\), so \(\angle XRP=15^\circ\). Therefore the right triangles \(RXP\) and \(QSR\) have equal \(15^\circ\) angles and equal hypotenuses \(RP=QR\). They are congruent by angle-angle-side.

The corresponding legs \(RX\) and \(QS\) are consequently equal. But \(RX=h\), while the horizontal segment \(QS\) spans the alley and has length \(w\). Hence \(w=h\).

The answer is \(\boxed{h}\), choice \(\boxed{E}\).
solutions.title: An equilateral triangle and congruent right triangles
